transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Occupational health suggested I come. I guess they’re concerned because I’ve been… skipping breakfast and lunch when I’m caught up in lab runs or exhibition work. Then when I do eat, I tend to keep it very small. Controlled, I suppose.
When you choose to eat very small amounts, is it because you're worried about gaining weight or do you feel like your body looks a certain way that you don't like?
I… yes, I suppose it is about the scale. If it goes up even a little, I feel this sudden panic, like I’m losing control or discipline. I don’t really like admitting that.
When you're feeling panicked about weight gain, do you ever make yourself sick, exercise excessively, or use laxatives or diet pills to try to control your weight?
I’m… not sure how to answer that. I don’t really do anything dramatic. I mostly just try to keep things limited.
Can you tell me if you’ve ever exercised intensely to try to control your weight or made yourself sick after eating to prevent gaining weight?

I don’t… I don’t really think of it that way. I haven’t made myself sick, no. Exercise… I mean, I move around for work sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m doing intense workouts to make up for eating. Mostly I just try not to eat too much in the first place.
Have you ever fasted or severely restricted your calorie intake to prevent weight gain?

Yes… I suppose so. I tend to push breakfast and lunch aside when I’m in the lab or tied up with work, and then when I finally do eat, I keep it very small. Controlled, I guess. Occupational health thought it was enough of a pattern to send me here.
Do you feel like your body is larger than it actually is, or do you feel like you need to lose weight even when others might see you as underweight?
I… yes, I suppose I do. When I look in the mirror before work, I don’t really see “thin.” I notice my stomach or my hips, mostly, and it makes me feel like I look… careless, or not serious enough.
Do you judge yourself or feel like you’re a worse person, less capable, or less valuable because of your weight or shape?

I wouldn’t say I’m… less valuable, exactly. But yes, I do judge myself. If I look in the mirror before going to the lab, I don’t really see thin. I notice my stomach or my hips, and it makes me feel like I look careless, or not serious enough.
Have you ever had episodes where you feel like you're eating a very large amount of food in a short period of time, and feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?
Not really. I mean… I don’t think so. I’m usually trying to keep it quite limited, so I can’t say I’ve had that feeling of eating a huge amount and not being able to stop.
Is your limited eating mainly about trying to control your weight or shape, or is it more about other factors like the way food feels, tastes, or smells, or just not being interested in food?
It’s… mostly about weight, I think. Or shape. If the scale goes up even a little, I feel this sudden panic, like I’m losing control of the discipline I’ve been trying to keep.
When you judge yourself based on your weight or shape, does it strongly affect how you see yourself overall, like influencing whether you feel good or bad about who you are?

Yes… more than I’d like to admit. If I look in the mirror before going to the lab, I don’t really see someone thin. I just focus on my stomach or my hips, and then I feel like I look… careless, or not serious enough. It kind of colors how I feel about myself.
Would you say that your overall sense of self-worth or how you judge yourself is strongly tied to your body shape or weight?

Yes… I think so. I don’t really like saying that, but if I see my stomach or hips looking a certain way, I feel like it means something about me… like I look careless, or not serious. It affects how I feel about myself more than it should.
Would you say that your weight or body shape has an outsize influence on how you see yourself, more than it should, to the point where it affects your daily life or decisions?

Yes… I think it does. I mean, I can be getting ready for the lab and look in the mirror, and instead of just seeing myself, I get stuck on my stomach or my hips. Then it feels like I look… careless, or not serious. It can affect the rest of my day more than I want it to.
Would you say that your evaluation of yourself — whether you feel good or bad about who you are — is heavily influenced by your body weight or shape?

Yes… it does. I know I’ve sort of said this already, but when I look in the mirror before work, I don’t really see myself clearly. I just notice my stomach or hips, and then I feel like I look careless or… not serious. It changes how I feel about myself.

Would you say that your overall sense of self-worth is largely defined by your body weight or shape, to the point where it significantly affects your confidence or how you carry yourself in daily life?

Yes… I guess so. I don’t really see myself the way other people might. Before I go to the lab, if I look in the mirror, I mostly notice my stomach or my hips, and then I feel like I look careless, or not serious. It does affect how I carry myself, even if I don’t like admitting that.
